name: Colorado
overview: Colorado Parks and Wildlife issues most limited deer, elk, pronghorn, moose, bear, bighorn sheep, mountain goat and turkey licenses through a primary draw in which each applicant lists up to four hunt codes per species, and preference points count only for the first choice. Deer, elk, pronghorn, bear and turkey are drawn by preference points (with a random hybrid draw for up to 20% of licenses in select high-demand deer, elk, pronghorn and bear hunts), while moose, Rocky Mountain bighorn sheep and mountain goat switch to weighted-random preference once an applicant holds three points, and desert bighorn is a pure random draw. Applicants must first buy a qualifying license and Habitat Stamp; licenses left after the primary draw go to a secondary draw without points and then to over-the-counter leftover sales, and CPW has approved draw changes taking effect in 2028.

species.drawSystemSummary: Limited elk licenses are awarded in CPW's primary draw by preference points: applicants with the most points for their first-choice hunt code draw first. In hunt codes that need 10+ resident preference points to draw (three-year rolling average, one-year lag), up to 20% of licenses may be issued by a random 'hybrid' draw among first-choice applicants with at least 5 points (p.19).
species.residentNote: Applicants must first buy a current qualifying license (e.g., annual small game: resident $38.49, nonresident $104.86) and, ages 18–64, a $12.76 Habitat Stamp; the application fee is $8.93 resident / $11.49 nonresident per species. Preference points are used only in the primary draw and only for first choices; an applicant who does not draw a first-choice license gains one point, and all points for the species reset to zero when a first-choice license is drawn (p.9).
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents may receive up to 20% of the licenses in hunt codes that needed 6+ points for an adult resident to draw (marked '+' in the brochure) and up to 25% in others; the cap can rise if licenses remain after all resident first choices are drawn, and it does not apply to private-land-only or Ranching for Wildlife licenses (p.4). Nonresidents can no longer buy over-the-counter archery elk licenses west of I-25 or in GMU 140; limited nonresident archery hunt codes are offered in the draw instead (2026 brochure p.1).
species.otcSummary: 2026: unlimited OTC archery licenses for either-sex (E-E-000-U1-A) and antlerless (E-F-000-U1-A) elk are resident-only in the listed GMUs; nonresidents may hunt OTC archery only east of I-25 (E-E-087-U1-A, E-F-133-U1-A). Unlimited OTC bull licenses for the 2nd and 3rd rifle seasons (E-M-000-U2-R, E-M-000-U3-R) in listed GMUs, plus OTC plains either-sex rifle and GMU 128 bull rifle licenses. OTC sales opened Aug. 4, 2026. CPW's Commission approved draw-process changes that take effect in 2028 (cpw.state.co.us/2028-draw).

coverage.notes: 4917 hunt-code rows (2022: 862, 2023: 1003, 2024: 990, 2025: 1023, 2026: 1039). Counts are CPW primary-draw, first-choice results from the Draw Recap reports. resident/nonresident = CPW's adult columns; total = adult + youth general applications (landowner LPP vouchers excluded; youth and LPP numbers are in each row's note). Odds are computed as drawn / applicants (oddsComputed). minPoints = CPW's published 'Drawn Out At' level for adults; hybrid-draw winners can draw below it, which shows in byPoints. Hunt codes are printed without dashes as in the recap (EE001E1R = E-E-001-E1-R); units = the GMU in the hunt code, which CPW defines as the lowest valid GMU, so multi-GMU hunts cover more units than listed. Hunt codes CPW reports together as a float group are one row with space-separated codes. The preference-point-only code (e.g. EP99999P) is excluded; with it, the hunt-code sums reproduce CPW's statewide first-choice applicant totals exactly, and drawn totals match exactly, for every year. Secondary-draw results are not included. For the latest year, seasonDates/seasonRanges are the hunt code's dates in CPW's Chapter W-2 (big game) or W-3 (turkey) season tables, read by scripts/agency/colorado/seasons_parse.py; Ranching for Wildlife hunts, which the regulations do not date, use the brochure's RFW tables (seasonSourceId says which).
